answer_data: Reference state transition triggered by withdrawal
Retained pin value with a withdrawn marker
Statement that this model records the fact but performs no remediation

data_elements.name: Pin mode
data_elements.description: Whether the reference is live, version-pinned, digest-pinned or snapshot-pinned.

data_elements.name: Pinned version
data_elements.description: The endpoint version or revision label the reference is fixed to, recorded exactly as published by the endpoint owner.

data_elements.name: Content digest
data_elements.description: Digest algorithm and value that immutably bind the reference to specific content; compared on algorithm and value only.

data_elements.name: Declared compatibility range
data_elements.description: The issuer's declaration of which upstream revisions the assertion is claimed to cover, with the grammar used to express it.

data_elements.name: Snapshot reference
data_elements.description: Reference to an immutable snapshot of the endpoint held by an external system; a specialization of the live endpoint, not a copy owned here.

artifacts.name: Endpoint pin descriptor
artifacts.description: A descriptor attached to one role binding that fixes what the reference points at: pin mode, pinned version or digest, snapshot reference and declared compatibility range. It is a naming record only; it holds no endpoint content and triggers no fetch or verification.
media_or_form: structured sub-record of the assertion envelope
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified by the parent assertion identifier plus the role binding it qualifies; where the pin is digest-based, the digest algorithm and value provide a self-verifying secondary key. Never keyed by the endpoint's own identifier alone, since one endpoint may be pinned differently by many assertions.

findings.name: Epistemic, completeness and resolution states
findings.description: Silence must never become proof. SPDX separates an explicit NoneElement (no such relationship exists) from a NoAssertionElement (no assertion is being made), and its RelationshipCompleteness vocabulary separates complete, incomplete and noAssertion. CycloneDX encodes the same distinction in the opposite way - an empty dependency element means no dependencies, while an unrepresented component means unknown - so the two encodings are not interchangeable and a normalized epistemic state must be recorded explicitly. Reference resolution adds a further axis: resolved, unresolved or dangling, ambiguous, or withdrawn upstream, each carrying a verification time and a staleness horizon.

questions.text: Which epistemic state applies here: dependency asserted present, asserted absent, unknown, not assessed, or unresolved?
answer_data: Epistemic state code
Reason or method that produced the state
Explicit statement that the absence of a record is not the absent state

questions.text: Is the prerequisite set for this dependent declared exhaustive, known not to be exhaustive, or unqualified?
answer_data: Completeness qualifier value
Scope over which completeness is claimed
Issuer that stands behind the completeness claim

questions.text: When was this endpoint reference last verified, and after what interval is that observation treated as stale?
answer_data: Last-verified RFC 3339 timestamp
Staleness horizon as a duration
Derived stale flag and its recomputation rule

questions.text: How does the record distinguish an explicitly asserted independence from the mere absence of any assertion?
answer_data: Explicit independence marker and its issuer
Scope and relation type over which independence is claimed
Contrast case showing what an absent record means

questions.text: Which state is recorded when a prerequisite locator resolves to more than one candidate endpoint?
answer_data: Ambiguous resolution state code
Candidate locator list as reported by the external resolver
Statement that disambiguation is not performed by this model

data_elements.name: Epistemic state
data_elements.description: Normalized state of the claim: asserted-present, asserted-absent, unknown, not-assessed or unresolved. Absence of a record is never encoded as asserted-absent.

data_elements.name: Prerequisite completeness qualifier
data_elements.description: Whether the prerequisite set is complete, incomplete or unqualified, adopting the SPDX three-state vocabulary.

data_elements.name: Reference resolution state
data_elements.description: Reported outcome of an external resolver for a role-bound locator: resolved, unresolved or dangling, ambiguous, or withdrawn upstream.

data_elements.name: Last-verified time
data_elements.description: RFC 3339 instant at which the reference state was last confirmed by an external resolver.

data_elements.name: Staleness horizon
data_elements.description: Duration after which an unrefreshed verification is treated as stale, so that an old confirmation is not read as a current one.

artifacts.name: Explicit non-dependency statement
artifacts.description: An identified, attributed statement that a named dependent has no prerequisite of a given relation type within a stated scope - the positive form of absence, distinct from an unrecorded dependency. Follows the SPDX pattern in which an explicit none marker must stand alone and must not be combined with other targets.
media_or_form: explicit none marker in an exchange format
artifacts.identity_strategy: Uses the same identity priority and identifier space as an ordinary assertion envelope, keyed by dep-core-de-assertion-id; the dependent reference, relation type and scope together form the correlation key, and no prerequisite role binding is present.

layers.name: Relation shape and degenerate cases
layers.description: Arity, ordering, composite prerequisites and the degenerate shapes that a naive edge model silently mishandles.

findings.name: Arity, ordering, composite prerequisites and degenerate shapes
findings.description: SPDX gives one from element to one or more to elements, so one-to-one and one-to-many are native while many-to-one and many-to-many are expressed as multiple assertions sharing a prerequisite or a correlation key. TOSCA adds occurrence constraints for cardinality bounds. Ordering has no dependency-specific normative source: RDF Schema supplies rdf:Seq, where numerical ordering of membership properties is significant, and rdf:List, where ordering is structural, and these are adopted by analogy. CSAF shows that a composite of two products is given its own minted product identifier, which is why a composite prerequisite group is modelled here as a grouping over references rather than as a new endpoint. Self-dependencies, exact duplicates and reversed direction are recorded as detected shapes, never silently normalized away.

questions.text: Which arity pattern does this assertion express, and how are many-to-one and many-to-many cases carried?
answer_data: Arity pattern code
Number of dependent and prerequisite role bindings
Correlation key or group reference linking assertions that jointly express a wider arity

questions.text: When prerequisites are ordered, what carries the ordinal and what does that order actually mean?
answer_data: Ordinal per prerequisite binding
Declared meaning of the order (precedence, preference or fallback)
Statement of whether the order is significant or merely presentational

questions.text: How is a composite prerequisite group expressed without importing condition evaluation into this record?
answer_data: Group membership references
Combination operator code such as all-of or any-of
Reference to the condition facilities that hold any guard expression

questions.text: How are self-dependencies and exact-duplicate assertions detected and recorded rather than silently dropped?
answer_data: Self-reference flag where dependent and prerequisite locators are equivalent
Duplicate marker and the reference to the earlier assertion
Rule requiring the shape to be recorded, not discarded

questions.text: Which key decides that two assertion records express the same claim?
answer_data: Correlation key composition
Comparison level applied to each locator within the key
Treatment of records that match on key but differ on issuer or effective interval

data_elements.name: Arity pattern
data_elements.description: Declared shape of the assertion: one-to-one, one-to-many, many-to-one or many-to-many, where the latter two are carried across linked assertions.

data_elements.name: Prerequisite ordinal
data_elements.description: Ordinal attached to a prerequisite role binding when order is significant, together with the declared meaning of that order.

data_elements.name: Composite prerequisite group
data_elements.description: Grouping over prerequisite role bindings with a combination operator; guard logic and its evaluation are referenced from the model's condition facilities, not embedded here.

data_elements.name: Self-reference flag
data_elements.description: Set when the dependent and a prerequisite locator are equivalent at the recorded comparison level, so the degenerate shape is visible rather than hidden.

data_elements.name: Duplicate-of reference
data_elements.description: Reference to an earlier assertion carrying the same correlation key, recorded when a duplicate is admitted rather than rejected.

artifacts.name: Composite prerequisite group record
artifacts.description: A named grouping of two or more prerequisite role bindings treated as one prerequisite for the dependent, carrying membership, optional ordinals and a combination operator. It groups references only; it mints no endpoint and evaluates no condition.
media_or_form: ordered or unordered collection sub-record within the envelope
RDF collection or sequence over references
grouped rows in a prerequisite register
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified by the parent assertion identifier plus a stable group label unique within that assertion; the group never inherits or reuses a member endpoint's identifier, and if the composite ever needs standalone identity it must be minted by the endpoint model, not here.

functions.name: Record dependency assertion
functions.description: Create an identified dependency assertion envelope binding a dependent endpoint reference to one or more prerequisite endpoint references under a typed relation term, within a declared scope and effective interval.
inputs: Dependent endpoint locator and role binding
Prerequisite endpoint locators and role bindings
Relation-type term reference from a governed vocabulary
Adopting Dimension, tenant and applicability scope
outputs: Assertion envelope record at its first revision with an identifier assigned under the identity priority order
Correlation key for later duplicate and disagreement detection
preconditions: Each endpoint reference carries a scheme-qualified locator or an explicit host-scope flag
The relation-type term resolves in a vocabulary this model does not own
An identifier is obtainable at one of the three identity tiers
effects: A new assertion identity exists within the adopting Dimension's namespace
No endpoint is created, allocated, renamed, configured, deployed or invoked
No graph closure, impact score or authorization decision is produced

functions.name: Bind endpoint reference to a role
functions.description: Attach a scheme-qualified locator, optional sub-endpoint anchor and endpoint type reference to the dependent or a prerequisite role slot, recording the comparison level that will govern equivalence.
outputs: Role-bound endpoint reference within the envelope
Recorded locator scope flag and comparison level
preconditions: The role slot is vacant or the binding forms part of a new revision
The scheme is registered or its assignment rules are documented
Document-local references are rebound or explicitly marked host-scoped
effects: The reference is recorded without any attempt to dereference it
Endpoint identity, custody and configuration remain wholly external
Anchored sub-endpoints are addressed without minting new endpoint identifiers

functions.name: Pin endpoint reference
functions.description: Fix a role-bound reference to a specific endpoint version, content digest or snapshot, or declare it live, and record the issuer's compatibility range.
inputs: Pinned version, or digest algorithm and value, or snapshot reference
outputs: Pin descriptor attached to the role binding
Statement of what may change upstream without invalidating the assertion
preconditions: Digest algorithm is named from a registered hash-algorithm registry
Live mode carries no pinned value
Version labels are recorded exactly as published by the endpoint owner
effects: The reference becomes version-fixed or self-verifying by digest
No content is fetched, copied, cached or verified by this model
Upstream version creation and withdrawal remain owned by the endpoint owner

functions.name: Record reference state and staleness
functions.description: Record the epistemic, completeness and resolution states of an assertion and its references, together with the verification time and staleness horizon.
inputs: Resolution outcome reported by an external resolver
Completeness qualifier for the prerequisite set
outputs: Recorded epistemic, completeness and resolution states
Derived stale marker when verification is older than the horizon
preconditions: The resolution outcome originates from a resolver external to this model
Timestamps are RFC 3339 values with seconds and an explicit offset
The absence of a report is admissible only as not-assessed
effects: Unknown, not-assessed and unresolved remain distinguishable from asserted-absent
No resolution, scanning, discovery or disambiguation is performed here
Stale observations are marked rather than silently refreshed or deleted

functions.name: Declare explicit non-dependency
functions.description: Record an attributed statement that a dependent has no prerequisite of a given relation type within a stated scope, so that independence is asserted rather than inferred from silence.
outputs: Explicit non-dependency statement carrying its own assertion identifier
Correlation key over dependent, relation type and scope
preconditions: Issuer and authority basis are recorded
Scope and relation type are stated explicitly
No prerequisite role binding accompanies the negative marker
effects: An explicit negative claim exists that is distinguishable from an unrecorded dependency
Nothing is asserted about endpoints or relation types outside the declared scope
No inference of absence is created for any other dependent

functions.name: Normalize relation direction
functions.description: Map an imported relation term stated in a foreign direction onto the canonical dependent-to-prerequisite binding while preserving the original term and its native direction verbatim.
inputs: Imported relation term and its defining vocabulary
Published native direction of that term
outputs: Canonical role binding in the dependent-to-prerequisite direction
Preserved source term, native direction and reversal flag
preconditions: The native direction is documented by the source vocabulary
Terms with ambiguous or undocumented direction are rejected rather than guessed
The mapping rule used is itself referenceable
effects: Direction is normalized exactly once, at import
No vocabulary term is redefined, extended or republished
The original statement remains reconstructible from the preserved fields

functions.name: Revise, supersede or retract assertion
functions.description: Advance an assertion to a new revision, replace it with a successor identity, or retract it, keeping prior revisions readable and leaving both endpoints untouched.
outputs: New revision entry, or a successor assertion with supersession pointers in both directions
preconditions: The change is classified as revision-preserving or identity-breaking by the canonicalization rules
The record is not already in a terminal state
Competing assertions by other issuers are left untouched
effects: Prior revisions remain retrievable and the content digest chain stays verifiable
Retraction removes no endpoint and cancels no downstream consumer's own records
Erasure of tombstones is deferred to the adopting Dimension's retention policy

composition.target: Endpoint / resource model of the adopting Dimension (dependent and prerequisite subjects)
composition.purpose: Supply the endpoints that this mixin points at. This model carries role bindings, locators, pins and reported states only; endpoint creation, naming, custody, configuration, deployment, invocation, monitoring and disposition remain entirely with the target model.

composition.target: Dependency relation-type vocabulary or classifier registry
composition.purpose: Bind exactly one typed relation term per assertion. Term definition, native direction, versioning, deprecation and publication stay with the registry; this model records the term reference, the registry version and any reversal applied at import.

composition.target: Identifier, namespace and scheme registry authorities
composition.purpose: Govern the schemes and namespaces under which assertion identifiers and endpoint locators are minted, including persistence and uniqueness guarantees. This model records the scheme and locator; assignment, registration and resolution services stay with the authority.

composition.target: RFC 3339 timestamp profile of the adopting Dimension
composition.purpose: Fix the representation of declared-at, observed-at, recorded-at, effective interval and last-verified values. The alignment supplies representation only; the separation of event time from observation and ingestion time is stated locally because RFC 3339 does not define it.

composition.target: Graph traversal, closure and impact-computation model
composition.purpose: Consume assertions as edges and perform reachability, cycle detection, depth and blast-radius computation. This model supplies edge assertions, completeness qualifiers and declared propagation parameters only; it never computes, caches or scores a result.

Align the assertion envelope with the qualified-influence pattern and with bundles as identified, attributable sets of descriptions, so that provenance of the assertion itself is expressible. Activity, agent and plan lifecycles remain PROV's and are not re-implemented here.

composition.target: Change, release and version model of the endpoint owner
composition.purpose: Own creation, promotion and withdrawal of endpoint versions and snapshots. This model records the pin and the declared compatibility range and marks a reference withdrawn when told so; it never creates, promotes, migrates or remediates a version.

composition.target: Policy and authorization model of the adopting Dimension
composition.purpose: Decide and enforce who may read or write assertion records. This model declares access scopes and default visibility for its own records; evaluation, enforcement and any runtime decision belong wholly to the target and are never carried out here.

composition.target: Audit and event-record model of the adopting Dimension
composition.purpose: Capture and retain audit trails for reads, writes, supersessions and retractions of assertion records. This model states which facts an audit record should contain; capture, storage, tamper-evidence and retention of that trail are owned by the target.

composition.target: Bill-of-materials and relationship exchange formats (SPDX 3.0, CycloneDX / ECMA-424, CSAF 2.0)
composition.purpose: Interoperate with published relationship encodings for direction, arity, completeness and absence, and record where their conventions conflict. Alignment is claimed only where a mapping has been evidenced against a named version; no conformance to any of these formats is asserted.

Determine which concrete endpoint satisfies an abstract requirement and report resolution outcomes. This model records the resulting bound reference and the reported state; the matching algorithm, node filters and scan schedules belong to the target.

composition.target: Generic assertion / statement mixin of the adopting Dimension
composition.purpose: Specialize a generic identified, attributed, time-bounded statement into a dependency assertion by adding dependent and prerequisite roles, canonical direction, pins, arity and prerequisite completeness. Generic identity, attribution and disagreement machinery is inherited from the target, not restated here.

owner_package_requirements: The adopting Dimension must designate a named steward for the dependency assertion corpus who is accountable for identifier minting, canonicalization rules and the direction-normalization rule set, and who is distinct from any endpoint owner.

The Dimension must publish the identifier scheme or URN namespace used for assertion identifiers, its uniqueness and persistence rules, and the registered authority behind it, before any assertion leaves draft status.

The Dimension must nominate, for each admitted relation-type vocabulary, the registry version in force and the mapping to the canonical dependent-to-prerequisite direction, and must republish that mapping when the registry version changes.

The Dimension must state which external models own endpoints, graph closure and impact computation, policy evaluation, audit capture and retention execution, so that no consumer infers those capabilities from this model.
The Dimension must set the default staleness horizon and the default completeness qualifier applied when an issuer supplies neither.
dimension.namespace_guidance: Assertion identifiers are minted in a namespace owned by the adopting Dimension and kept strictly disjoint from endpoint identifier namespaces, so that no identifier can be read as either an assertion or an endpoint. Where a URN is used, its Namespace Identifier must be registered and the namespace must publish its own uniqueness and persistence rules; where an HTTP(S) IRI is used, the authority component must be one the Dimension controls or holds a durable delegation for. Locators for referenced endpoints are never rewritten into the Dimension's namespace: they are stored in the issuing authority's scheme with the scheme and the applied comparison level recorded. Document-local references imported from an exchange format are either rebound to a scheme-qualified locator or retained with an explicit host-scope flag and a host record reference, because such references are unique only inside their originating document.
registry_links: Vercy world-model registry entry vr.wm-xct-037 (record plane: world-model; navigation path NAV.XCT.DEP; domain tag XCT.DEP)
IANA Uniform Resource Identifier (URI) Schemes registry, for admitted locator schemes under RFC 3986
IANA Uniform Resource Names (URN) Namespaces registry, for Namespace Identifiers used in assertion and endpoint identifiers under RFC 8141
IANA Named Information Hash Algorithm registry, for digest algorithms admitted in immutable snapshot pins under RFC 6920
IANA Link Relation Types registry, as one admitted source of typed relation terms under RFC 8288

canonicalization_rules: Direction is normalized exactly once, at import: every assertion is stored in the canonical dependent-to-prerequisite direction, and the source vocabulary's term and native direction are retained verbatim alongside the reversal flag. Terms whose native direction is undocumented are rejected, never inferred.

Locator comparison uses the weakest sufficient rung of the RFC 3986 equivalence ladder and the applied rung is stored with the comparison; scheme-specific components that a namespace excludes from equivalence, such as URN r-, q- and f-components, are dropped before comparison and never used to distinguish two references.

The correlation key is computed over issuer, dependent locator, ordered prerequisite locators, relation-type term and effective-interval start, each normalized to its recorded comparison level; records matching on the key but differing on issuer are retained as parallel assertions and are never merged.

Absence encodings from exchange formats are normalized into the explicit epistemic state on import: an empty dependency element becomes asserted-absent, an omitted element becomes not-assessed, and an explicit no-assertion marker becomes unknown. The original encoding is retained so the mapping stays reversible.

Timestamps are canonicalized to RFC 3339 with seconds and an explicit offset; -00:00 is preserved where the source used it, because it means a known UTC instant with unknown local offset and is not equivalent to Z.
patch_rules: Changes to the dependent or prerequisite role bindings, the relation-type term, the canonical direction or the applicability scope are identity-breaking: they require a new assertion identifier with supersession pointers in both directions, not an in-place revision.

Changes to pins, compatibility ranges, epistemic or resolution states, staleness horizons, ordinals and non-normative descriptions are revision-preserving: they advance the revision ordinal on the same assertion identity.
Every patch records the issuer, the declared-at time and the recorded-at time of the patch, and recomputes the content digest; a patch that would leave the digest unchanged is rejected as a no-op.
Retraction is a patch to a terminal state, not a deletion: the record keeps its identifier, its final revision and the retraction reason, and prior revisions remain readable.
A patch never alters another issuer's assertion, and never edits an endpoint, an endpoint version or any record owned by a referenced model.
compatibility_rules: Consumers must treat the assertion identifier as opaque and must not parse a revision, date, endpoint name or direction out of it.

Adding a new optional field, a new epistemic-state code or a new relation-type binding is backward compatible; removing a field, narrowing a cardinality, reversing the canonical direction or redefining an existing state code is breaking and requires a new model version.
An unrecognised epistemic state, completeness qualifier or pin mode must be treated as unknown and must never be downgraded to asserted-absent.

Claimed alignment with an exchange format is versioned against a specific format version; when that version changes, the alignment is re-evidenced before it is re-asserted, and unverified mappings are recorded as gaps rather than published as conformance.

identity_priority: Authoritative master-system identifier: where a system of record already governs this dependency assertion, its assertion key is adopted verbatim and unmodified as the primary identifier, and no second identifier is minted.

Governed global identifier or IRI: a URI/IRI or a URN minted under a registered scheme or IANA-registered Namespace Identifier whose assigning authority, uniqueness rules and persistence commitments are published.

UUID or ULID assigned by the adopting Dimension: an opaque locally minted identifier, preferring the time-ordered UUID form, used only when neither a master-system identifier nor a governed global identifier exists; treated as opaque and never parsed for embedded meaning.

Never an identifier: a date, an effective interval, a revision label, a content digest alone, or an endpoint pair. A deterministic correlation key over issuer, roles, relation type and effective start may be recorded to recognise the same claim across hosts, but it is a correlation aid and never replaces the assertion identifier.
Endpoint identifiers are never reused as assertion identifiers, and an assertion identifier is never presented as denoting either endpoint.
artifact_rules.timestamp_rule: All time values are recorded as RFC 3339 date-time strings that include seconds and an explicit numeric UTC offset or the literal Z; the offset -00:00 is used only for a known UTC instant whose local offset is unknown and is not treated as equivalent to Z or +00:00. Event time and observation or ingestion time are recorded separately and are never collapsed: observed_at is the event time at which the dependency condition was seen to hold at the endpoints, declared_at is the instant the issuer made the claim, and recorded_at is the observation or ingestion time at which the record entered this model. When these values differ, all differing values are retained, recorded_at is never back-dated to match observed_at, and the field used for ordering competing records is stated explicitly on the record.
artifact_rules.serial_naming_rule: Serial artifacts are the assertion revision entries. Each is named as the parent assertion identifier followed by a revision segment and a zero-padded monotonic ordinal, for example <assertion-identifier>/rev/0007. Ordinals are allocated per assertion identity, start at 1, increase by one, are never reused after retraction, and never contain a date, an endpoint name or a status word. Non-serial artifacts - the assertion envelope record, the endpoint pin descriptor, the explicit non-dependency statement and the composite prerequisite group - are named by their identity strategy and carry no ordinal.
artifact_rules.integrity_rule: Every artifact carries a content digest computed over its canonicalized form with the digest field itself and any purely transport metadata excluded, using an algorithm drawn from a registered hash-algorithm registry and expressed as algorithm plus value so that it is comparable on those two components alone. Any change to role bindings, relation type, canonical direction, pins, applicability scope or effective interval invalidates the digest and forces a new revision or a new assertion identity as the patch rules require. Digests of referenced endpoint content are recorded as naming information only: this model neither fetches nor verifies endpoint content, and verification is performed by the consumer that dereferences the reference.

policies: Silence is never evidence: the absence of an assertion record must never be rendered, exported or interpreted as an assertion that no dependency exists. Only an explicit non-dependency statement, attributed and scoped, carries that meaning.

No assertion confers any right, claim or capability over either endpoint. Recording, revising or retracting an assertion must not create, allocate, rename, merge, configure, deploy, invoke, monitor or dispose of an endpoint, and must not be presented to a consumer as authorisation to do so.

Direction is normalized once and the source term is preserved: an imported relation with undocumented or ambiguous native direction is rejected with a recorded reason rather than assigned a direction by inference.
Competing assertions coexist: disagreement between issuers is recorded as parallel assertions with their attributions intact, and this model publishes no adjudication verdict.
Alignment is not conformance: mappings to external standards are recorded with the specific standard version they were evidenced against, and any unverified mapping is published as a gap.
Every stated epistemic state must be traceable to an issuer and a time; a state that cannot be attributed is recorded as not-assessed rather than defaulted to a positive or negative claim.

read: Reading an assertion returns the envelope with its identifier, issuer, three timestamps, effective interval, canonical direction, role bindings, relation-type term, epistemic and completeness states, and the current revision label.
A read must surface the staleness marker alongside any resolution state, so that an old confirmation is never presented as a current one.
Reads never dereference endpoint locators, never resolve pins and never expand transitive prerequisites; a consumer wanting closure must call the referenced graph model.
A read of a superseded or retracted record returns it with its terminal status and its successor pointer rather than silently redirecting to the successor.
create: Creation requires an issuer reference, a declared-at time, a canonical direction with at least one dependent and one prerequisite binding (or an explicit non-dependency marker), a relation-type term reference and an applicability scope.
An identifier is assigned strictly by the identity priority order; where a master-system identifier exists it is adopted verbatim and no local identifier is minted.

Creation is idempotent against the correlation key for the same issuer: a repeated submission returns the existing assertion rather than creating a duplicate, while a submission from a different issuer creates a parallel assertion.
Records failing direction, scheme or attribution preconditions are created in draft or quarantined with a recorded reason; they are never silently discarded.
update: Identity-breaking changes are performed as supersession by a new assertion identity with pointers in both directions, never as an in-place edit.
Revision-preserving changes advance the revision ordinal, append a revision entry and recompute the content digest.
Updates never modify another issuer's assertion, an endpoint record, an endpoint version or any record owned by a referenced model.
Every update records who made it, the declared-at time of the change and the recorded-at time of ingestion.
delete: Delete is soft by default and is expressed as retraction: the record moves to a terminal retracted status and a tombstone is retained holding the assertion identifier, issuer reference, canonical direction, final revision label, retraction reason, retraction timestamp and content digest. Downstream consumers may already hold resolved copies, so the identifier must remain resolvable to its tombstone.

Hard erasure of a tombstone is permitted only under the adopting Dimension's records-retention and data-protection policy. This model defines only the tombstone shape and the minimum fields that must survive; retention periods, legal hold, erasure scheduling and erasure execution are owned by the adopting Dimension's retention policy and by the referenced audit and event-record model, which also holds the record of the erasure itself.

Deleting or retracting an assertion never deletes, deallocates, deprecates or modifies either endpoint; endpoint disposition is owned entirely by the referenced endpoint or resource model, and this model neither triggers nor confirms it.

Deleting an assertion does not create an assertion of independence: after retraction the epistemic state for that dependent and relation type reverts to not-assessed unless an explicit non-dependency statement is issued.
Cascade deletion is prohibited: retracting one assertion never removes parallel assertions by other issuers, referencing assertions, or any record owned by a referenced model.

roles.name: Assertion issuer
responsibilities: State the dependency claim with a canonical direction, applicability scope and effective interval
Supply attribution, the declared-at time and, where a real observation exists, the observed-at time
Declare the completeness qualifier for a prerequisite set, or explicitly leave it unqualified
Retract or supersede claims found to be mistaken rather than letting them expire silently

roles.name: Dependency model steward (designated by the adopting Dimension)
responsibilities: Own identifier minting, the namespace, canonicalization rules and the direction-normalization rule set
Admit relation-type vocabularies and maintain the direction mappings and registry versions in force
Adjudicate nothing between issuers, but ensure disagreements are recorded as parallel assertions with attribution intact
Maintain the tombstone shape and hand retention and erasure execution to the Dimension's retention policy

roles.name: Endpoint reference custodian
responsibilities: Keep locators, schemes and namespaces for referenced endpoints correct and rebind imported document-local references
Record pins, compatibility ranges and withdrawn-upstream markers as reported by the endpoint owner
Escalate endpoint changes to the endpoint owner rather than acting on the endpoint
Confirm that no local record implies custody of an endpoint this model only references

roles.name: Reference verification operator
responsibilities: Submit resolution outcomes from an external resolver, with verification timestamps
Apply staleness horizons and mark observations stale rather than refreshing them silently
Record ambiguous resolution without disambiguating it
Ensure a missing report is recorded as not-assessed and never as asserted-absent

roles.name: Interoperability liaison
responsibilities: Maintain evidenced mappings to external relationship encodings against specific standard versions
Record conflicts between encodings of direction, arity, completeness and absence
Publish unverified mappings as gaps rather than as conformance claims
Re-evidence alignments when an external standard version changes

access.default_rule: Assertion records are readable by principals holding read access to both the dependent and the prerequisite endpoint within the same adopting Dimension and tenant; write access is limited to the recorded issuer and the dependency model steward. This model declares the scopes and the default only - every access decision is evaluated and enforced by the referenced policy and authorization model, and this model neither evaluates nor enforces any rule.
exceptions: A principal entitled to see only one endpoint may be shown a redacted assertion in which the counterpart locator is replaced by an opacity marker, provided the epistemic state, direction and existence of the assertion remain visible so that redaction is never mistaken for absence.

Assertions whose applicability scope names a restricted jurisdiction or a restricted purpose may be withheld from cross-tenant reads; the withholding must be recorded as restricted rather than rendered as not-assessed.
Explicit non-dependency statements are readable wherever the corresponding positive assertion would be readable, since withholding them would reintroduce silence as evidence.
Tombstones remain readable to principals who could read the record before retraction, so that a resolved identifier does not become an unexplained dangling reference.
Emergency read-through for incident handling is granted by the referenced policy model, not by this model, and is recorded as an exception on the reading side.
audit_requirements: Each read, create, update, supersession, retraction and erasure of an assertion record should be captured with the principal, the assertion identifier, the revision label, the RFC 3339 event time and the recorded ingestion time.
Redactions and withholdings should be captured with the exception invoked and the scope applied, so that a redacted view can later be distinguished from a genuinely empty result.
Direction reversals applied at import, and rejections of relations with undocumented native direction, should be captured with the mapping rule reference.

Capture, storage, retention, tamper-evidence and replay of these audit records are owned wholly by the referenced audit and event-record model; this model states only which facts such a record should contain and holds no audit trail of its own.

required_fields: Referenced models that own endpoints, graph closure, impact computation, policy evaluation, audit capture and retention execution
read_order: AGENTS.md - identify the model, its type, and the URLs for specification, storage type, interface and processes before touching any record
Specification URL - read the scope statement, boundary notes and the canonical dependent-to-prerequisite direction, and confirm what this model does not own
Storage type URL - learn the projection in use (document, graph, tabular or version-controlled) and confirm the projection carries assertion identity, revision label and content digest
Interface URL - learn how to read, create, revise, supersede and retract assertions, and confirm that no interface operation resolves locators, computes closure or enforces policy
Processes URL - follow the canonicalization, direction-normalization, staleness and retention procedures before writing
Referenced-model bootstrap files - resolve the endpoint, vocabulary, graph and impact, policy and audit models before interpreting any assertion as actionable

coverage.claim: This research derives a defensible, format-neutral structure for the dependency assertion envelope and its endpoint reference boundary in WM-XCT-037, grounded in primary W3C, IETF, OASIS, SPDX, Ecma/CycloneDX and CISA sources. Direction, arity, completeness and the separation of absence from ignorance are supported by normative text; assertion identity is deliberately modelled as weak and host-dependent because no consulted source grants a dependency statement strong independent identity. Ordering, jurisdiction scoping and the confidentiality of dependency data rest on analogical or unverified support and are recorded as gaps rather than presented as canonical.

checklist.notes: Three-tier identity priority with the authoritative master-system identifier first; assertion identity kept disjoint from endpoint identity; weak host-dependent identity evidenced by PROV's optional qualified-relation identifier, RDF blank nodes being explicitly non-persistent and non-portable, and CycloneDX bom-ref uniqueness being enforced only within the root bom element.

Draft, active, superseded, retracted and expired states with identity-breaking versus revision-preserving patch rules, serial revision entries and bidirectional supersession pointers, aligned to PROV revision semantics. Only the assertion record's own lifecycle is modelled; endpoint lifecycle is explicitly out of scope.

Canonical dependent-to-prerequisite direction fixed and evidenced against TOSCA DependsOn, SPDX from/to and CycloneDX dependsOn; source vocabulary terms and native directions preserved verbatim; typed relation terms bound by reference only, never authored here.

Declared-at, observed-at and recorded-at kept distinct; RFC 3339 with seconds and explicit offset; -00:00 preserved as a distinct meaning; effective interval carried on the assertion following SPDX startTime and endTime; staleness horizons applied to verification.

Issuer and observing agent recorded separately, authority basis referenced, parallel assertions from different issuers coexist without adjudication following PROV's multiple-accounts model, and content digests make revisions verifiable.

Adopting Dimension and tenant own the record; both endpoints are externally owned throughout. Steward, issuer, custodian, verification operator and liaison roles separate record stewardship from endpoint custody.

Locator equivalence uses the RFC 3986 comparison ladder with the applied rung recorded, URN components excluded from equivalence are dropped, self-reference and duplicate shapes must be recorded rather than dropped, and relations with undocumented native direction are rejected.

Default rule requires read access to both endpoints; scopes cover bundle, layer, finding and artifact; redaction must preserve the visible existence of the assertion. Evaluation and enforcement are explicitly owned by the referenced policy model.

Soft delete by retraction with a tombstone retaining identifier, issuer, direction, final revision, reason, timestamp and digest; cascade deletion prohibited; retraction never implies independence. Retention periods, legal hold and erasure execution are owned by the adopting Dimension's retention policy and the referenced audit model.

Mappings evidenced against SPDX 3.0.1, CycloneDX 1.6 / ECMA-424, CSAF 2.0, TOSCA 1.3 and RFC 8288, with the absence-encoding conflict normalized reversibly on import. Alignment is claimed per standard version; no conformance is asserted.

A single canonical direction is fixed locally because no consulted source establishes a universal one; CSAF categories such as installed_on and the RFC 8288 deprecation of rev are the counterexamples that force normalization plus verbatim preservation of the source term.

One-to-one and one-to-many are directly supported by SPDX from/to cardinality and TOSCA occurrences; many-to-one and many-to-many are carried across linked assertions, which is a local construction. Ordering rests only on rdf:Seq and rdf:List by analogy - no dependency-specific normative source for prerequisite ordering was found.

Five distinct states normalized on import, evidenced by SPDX NoneElement versus NoAssertionElement, the three-value RelationshipCompleteness vocabulary and CycloneDX's inverse encoding of empty versus omitted; policy forbids rendering silence as absence.

Live, version, digest and snapshot pin modes with RFC 6920 content-addressed naming and PROV specialization as the alignment; dereference and verification remain the consumer's, and withdrawn upstream revisions are recorded, not remediated.

Jurisdiction and declared purpose are modelled as opaque codes bound to external registries. No primary source was verified that governs jurisdictional scoping or disclosure restriction of dependency assertions, so the field shape is asserted without normative backing.

The distinction between unknown to the issuer and known but deliberately withheld is operationally important and appears in secondary reporting on current SBOM guidance, but the primary CISA text could not be retrieved in machine-readable form in this research; only the document's identity and date were verified.

known_omissions: The evidence-grading and confidence vocabulary attached to an assertion is referenced but not enumerated; no primary source was found that grades dependency evidence, so no scale is proposed.

Declared impact-propagation parameters are named in the model boundary but no propagation semantics, criticality scale or blast-radius vocabulary is proposed, because every consulted source leaves computation to the consumer.
No cycle, self-loop or contradiction resolution procedure is defined: degenerate shapes are recorded and surfaced, and resolution is left to the referenced graph model.
Cryptographic signing of assertion envelopes is not specified beyond the content digest; signature suites, key management and trust anchors were not researched.
Cross-Dimension federation of assertion identifiers, including how two Dimensions recognise the same claim, is not resolved beyond the correlation key.
Rate, volume and scale characteristics of large assertion corpora, and any resulting partitioning conventions, were not investigated.
No mapping to project-scheduling dependency types such as finish-to-start and its variants was attempted; no accessible primary source for them was found in this research.
conflicts: Direction is not universal across sources. TOSCA DependsOn, SPDX from/to and CycloneDX dependsOn all read dependent-to-prerequisite, but CSAF categories such as installed_on invert the intuitive reading, and RFC 8288 deprecated the reversed rev parameter in favour of defining separate relation types. A single canonical direction is therefore a local normalization rule, and the source term must be preserved.

Absence and ignorance are encoded inversely. SPDX marks explicit absence with a NoneElement in the to property and ignorance with a NoAssertionElement, while CycloneDX marks absence by declaring an empty dependency element and ignorance by omitting the component from the graph. Round-tripping between them without an explicit normalized state silently converts one into the other.

The CycloneDX absence rule has drifted in strength across versions: the 1.6 XSD documentation uses SHOULD for declaring components without dependencies as empty elements, while widely quoted earlier-version wording uses MUST, and the project has recorded inconsistency between its JSON and XSD dependency definitions. Any conformance claim must name a specific schema version.

Endpoint reference portability differs by source. A CycloneDX bom-ref is unique only within the root bom element, SPDX uses IRI-based element identifiers, and RDF blank node identifiers are explicitly not persistent or portable. Imported references cannot be treated as globally meaningful without rebinding.

Statement-level identity is optional in the standards that come closest. PROV allows but does not require an identifier on a qualified influence, and RDF reification provides no identity guarantee at all, so a dependency assertion has no strong identity unless one is minted - which conflicts with any downstream assumption that assertions are globally addressable.

RFC 3339 is updated by RFC 9557, which adds extensions beyond the base offset representation. Records carrying extended forms may not compare equal under a strict RFC 3339 profile, so the profile version in force must be stated by the adopting Dimension.
regional_assumptions: Jurisdiction is treated as an opaque code bound to an external registry. No region-specific regime governing the disclosure, retention or cross-border transfer of dependency assertions was verified against a primary source in this research, so no regional rule is asserted.

The 2025 CISA minimum-elements guidance is a United States federal instrument and was in a public comment period at the cited date; it is used only as corroboration that dependency relationship data and explicit unknowns are treated as required transparency elements, and it is not treated as globally binding.

Timestamps assume the adopting Dimension operates a single RFC 3339 profile across tenants; deployments spanning regions with differing local-offset recording practice must state whether -00:00 is admitted, since it carries a distinct meaning from Z.
Relation-type vocabularies admitted by a Dimension may be region- or sector-specific; the direction mapping is evidenced per vocabulary version and is not assumed to transfer between sectors.
adversarial_checks: Searched for a normative source establishing one universal dependency direction and found none: TOSCA, SPDX and CycloneDX agree, but CSAF categories invert and RFC 8288 deprecated reversed relations rather than standardising them. The attractive claim of an inherent direction was rejected; direction is a local normalization with mandatory preservation of the source term.

Tested whether the absence of an assertion is ever normatively equivalent to an assertion of no dependency. SPDX separates NoneElement from NoAssertionElement and adds a three-value completeness vocabulary, and CycloneDX separates empty-element from omitted, but in the opposite direction. Every encoding relying on silence was rejected and an explicit epistemic state was made mandatory.

Tested whether the assertion could be given strong independent identity. PROV makes the qualified-relation identifier optional, RDF reification guarantees no identity, RDF blank nodes are explicitly non-portable and bom-ref is document-local. The claim of globally strong assertion identity was rejected in favour of explicit weak, host-dependent identity with a stated host scope and correlation key.

Tested the temptation to model transitive closure, depth or blast radius locally, since dependency data is normally consumed as a graph. No consulted source places closure on the individual relationship - SPDX puts completeness on the single relationship and CycloneDX leaves graph assembly to the consumer - so closure and impact computation were pushed to a REFERENCE link and named in out_of_scope.

Tested whether recording a content digest implies ownership of integrity verification. RFC 6920 makes clear that such a name identifies content but does not locate it, and that dereference is performed by the entity resolving the name, so the model records naming information only and disclaims fetching and verification.

Tested whether declaring access scopes, exceptions and audit expectations amounts to owning enforcement. It does not: the default rule, exceptions and audit field list are declarations about this model's own records, while evaluation, enforcement, audit capture and erasure execution are each assigned to a referenced model in the composition ledger and repeated in the delete rules.

Tested whether the composite prerequisite group quietly mints a new endpoint. CSAF mints a new product identifier for a combination, which shows the temptation is real; the group was therefore constrained to grouping references within one assertion, with any standalone composite identity explicitly deferred to the endpoint model.
